summary: Green Butte platform in the Deschutes National Forest, dated to 1990 for the Spring Butte rebuild; still standing but weakening on a May 2023 visit.

facts.design: Wooden platform, five or six feet tall (sources differ)
facts.status_note: Still standing but weakened on a May 2023 visit; the register says removed circa 2000; no source after May 2023 found

access.note: Reached by Deschutes National Forest roads and a short user trail; the trip report describes no closure of the platform

visit.trail_note: Walk up from the signed NF-720 junction; a higher-clearance vehicle can go farther; a small user trail leads from the end of the road to the platform. The trip report warns heavy snow will most likely bring it down.

events.note: Six-foot wooden platform, used while the Spring Butte lookout was being reconstructed (firelookout.com and The Roaming Civic)

Lightning fire started on the slope in August 2022 and burned about 23 acres around the top of the butte
Trip report visit on May 15, 2023: platform still standing among brush but weakened

corrections.why: A May 15, 2023 visit found the platform still standing among brush, though weakened. The register's removal date of circa 2000 is contradicted by that visit.
Firelookout.com and The Roaming Civic both give 1990 and tie the platform to the Spring Butte rebuild; the register's circa 1998 date conflicts with both.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: Register says circa 1998; firelookout.com and The Roaming Civic say 1990. The register's wording places the platform after the new Spring Butte tower was ready, while the other two accounts place it during the rebuild. NHLR dates the new Spring Butte tower to 1991 and 1992.
Register says five feet; firelookout.com and The Roaming Civic say six feet. The story says five to six feet and the record gives no single height_m.
Register says removed around 2000; the May 2023 trip report says still standing. The story reports both.
Register gives 5,754 ft (1,754 m); firelookout.com gives 5798 ft. The brief keeps the register value.

notes_for_editor: The brief's gone status conflicts with a May 2023 first-hand visit, and I proposed standing (weakened) as a correction; the register's circa 2000 removal is still reported in the story. Build year (1990 vs circa 1998) and height (five vs six feet) conflict. The Oregon Lookouts Lake County page (green-butte1.html) has only a heading for this site, so it adds nothing. No source after May 2023 was found, so the current condition is unknown and the platform may have fallen since. The trip report's geocacher report is secondhand and is labelled as such in the story. The access note comes from the trip report; no official closure or access source was checked.
